description: Conversational learning cards with subtitle, body paragraphs, and takeaway per card.

article.title: How to Do What You Love
article.author: Paul Graham

cards.title: Career Capital Comes Before Freedom
cards.subtitle: Most people want autonomy early, but autonomy is earned through rare skills.
body: If you become unusually good at useful work, you gain leverage over role, pay, and location.
Chasing passion without building capability often leads to fragile choices. Capability first makes later choices wider.
cards.takeaway: Build assets in yourself before demanding flexibility.

cards.title: Job Titles Can Distract From Skill Growth
cards.subtitle: A better title can feel like progress even when your learning has stalled.
body: Two years in a hard role with strong mentorship can beat a quick promotion in a low-growth environment.
Focus on what you are becoming, not just what your role is called.

cards.title: Mentors Shorten the Learning Curve
cards.subtitle: Good mentors do more than advice; they improve your standards and feedback speed.
body: A simple review from someone experienced can save months of avoidable mistakes.
You do not need one perfect mentor. Build a small bench of people strong in different areas.
cards.takeaway: Borrowing perspective is a career accelerator.

cards.title: Visibility Matters Alongside Quality
cards.subtitle: Great work that nobody sees rarely changes your opportunities.
body: Many professionals assume quality alone gets noticed. In practice, clear communication and visibility matter too.
Share outcomes, write concise updates, and make your impact legible to decision makers.
cards.takeaway: Do good work, then make it findable.

cards.title: Burnout Looks Like Ambition Until It Breaks
cards.subtitle: Sustained overwork can look admirable right before performance drops hard.
body: When recovery disappears, decision quality and creativity decline even if hours stay high.
Long careers reward pacing, boundaries, and renewal, not permanent sprint mode.
cards.takeaway: Treat energy like a strategic resource.

cards.title: Networking Is Relationship, Not Extraction
cards.subtitle: People can sense when outreach is purely transactional.
body: Useful networks are built by helping, following up, and staying in touch before you need anything.
Small acts of reliability compound into trust. Trust turns into opportunities later.

cards.title: Your Portfolio Should Tell a Story
cards.subtitle: Random achievements are less persuasive than a clear narrative of strengths.
body: When your projects connect to a theme, employers can quickly see where you create outsized value.
Curate your body of work intentionally. Show decisions, outcomes, and lessons.
cards.takeaway: Coherence makes talent easier to trust.

cards.title: Quitting Can Be a Strategic Move
cards.subtitle: Staying too long in a poor-fit role can cost more than a carefully timed exit.
body: If learning is flat, values are misaligned, and health is declining, persistence may be expensive.
Leaving is not failure when it protects long-term growth and motivation.
cards.takeaway: Endings can be part of good strategy.
